rules.text: Flag as anomaly if the bag contains loose hardware components (bolts, nuts, washers) instead of a single fastener assembly.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly assumed loose parts were normal variation. This rule explicitly defines the presence of unattached components as an anomaly, correcting the underprediction.

rules.text: Treat wire color variations as normal if the reference profiler explicitly lists color as an allowed variation for the product class.
rules.justification: The agent initially flagged the wire color difference as a defect. This rule ensures that when the profiler confirms color is a valid variation, the agent correctly classifies the item as normal.

rules.text: If the image contains a uniform mesh pattern instead of the expected splicing connectors, classify as anomaly.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the missing object but was refuted. This rule explicitly defines the mesh pattern as an anomaly mode, preventing refutation when the expected object is absent.

rules.text: Treat wire color variation as a normal attribute for splicing connectors, regardless of connector housing color.
rules.justification: The agent initially flagged the blue wire as an anomaly due to color mismatch with orange references. This rule explicitly defines wire color as a tolerated variation, preventing false positives.

rules.text: Do not flag single-wire assemblies as anomalies if the connector housing is intact and the wire is properly seated.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly assumed a fixed 3-wire structure. This rule clarifies that single-wire variants are valid normal configurations, preventing false positives based on wire count alone.

rules.text: Classify as anomaly if the bottle surface is completely devoid of any label, regardless of allowed content variations.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the missing label but lowered the score due to uncertainty. This rule explicitly defines total label absence as a definitive anomaly, overriding content variation tolerances.

rules.text: Treat variations in label iconography (e.g., fruit type) and liquid color as normal if explicitly permitted by reference data.
rules.justification: The agent initially flagged the banana icon and white liquid as anomalies. This rule clarifies that such visual differences are acceptable normal variations when validated by reference profilers, preventing false positives.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if the liquid color inside the bottle contradicts the fruit depicted on the label.
rules.justification: The agent hesitated despite clear visual evidence of white liquid in a bottle labeled with an orange. This rule explicitly links liquid color to label content to resolve such semantic inconsistencies.

rules.text: Treat variations in fruit iconography and liquid color as normal if explicitly permitted by the reference profiler.
rules.justification: The agent initially flagged the cherry icon and red liquid as defects. This rule clarifies that such variations are acceptable when validated by the reference profiler, preventing false positives.

rules.text: If the label icon depicts a fruit that does not match the liquid's color or implied flavor, classify as anomaly.
rules.justification: The agent hesitated despite the clear mismatch between the cherry icon and the red liquid. This rule explicitly flags such semantic inconsistencies as anomalies, preventing future uncertainty.

rules.text: Treat any visible tear, rip, or physical damage to the main product label as a definitive anomaly.
rules.justification: The agent initially detected the torn label but lowered its score. This rule reinforces that physical label damage is a critical defect, ensuring high anomaly scores for such cases.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if granola and dried fruit occupy the left compartment while fresh fruit occupies the right compartment.
rules.justification: The agent correctly identified the layout inversion but failed to commit to the anomaly label. This rule explicitly defines the observed left-right swap as a definitive defect, preventing future uncertainty.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if any compartment contains more than one pushpin, regardless of orientation or pin condition.
rules.justification: The agent incorrectly classified the image as normal because it focused on orientation and pin integrity. The actual anomaly is the presence of multiple pins in several compartments, which violates the expected one-pin-per-compartment rule.

rules.text: Classify as normal if pushpins are intact and present, even if randomly oriented or scattered within container compartments.
rules.justification: The agent hesitated due to the disorganized arrangement of pins. This rule clarifies that random orientation within a container is a normal variation, not an anomaly.

rules.text: Treat random orientation of pushpins within compartments as normal variation, provided pins are intact and undamaged.
rules.justification: The agent flagged the varied pin orientations as a potential anomaly. This rule clarifies that orientation is irrelevant to the defect status, resolving the false positive.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if any compartment contains more than one pushpin, as standard configuration requires exactly one per slot.
rules.justification: The agent missed the anomaly because it focused on missing or damaged pins. This rule explicitly defines overcrowding (multiple pins per slot) as a defect, correcting the oversight.

rules.text: Classify as normal if pushpins are intact and present, even if randomly oriented or scattered within container compartments.
rules.justification: The agent hesitated due to the disordered arrangement of pins. This rule clarifies that random orientation within a container is a normal variation, not an anomaly.

rules.text: Classify as normal if pins are intact and fully present, regardless of random orientation or rotation within compartments.
rules.justification: The agent overpredicted anomaly (0.5) due to random pin orientations. This rule clarifies that orientation variance is acceptable for intact pins, reducing false positives.

rules.text: Flag as anomaly if any pushpin is oriented vertically (head-up or head-down) instead of lying flat horizontally.
rules.justification: The agent missed the anomaly because it focused on object presence rather than orientation. The vertical pins in the top-right and bottom-right compartments deviate from the standard horizontal layout.

rules.text: Treat variations in pushpin orientation (vertical, horizontal, tilted) within a grid cell as normal, provided the pin is intact.
rules.justification: The agent's uncertainty likely stemmed from the non-uniform orientation of pins. This rule explicitly defines orientation variance as a normal characteristic, preventing false anomaly flags for intact pins.
